name: doc-pagination
purpose: The previous / next pair that closes a documentation page. Each side is a link carrying an eyebrow and the destination's title; a side with no neighbour leaves its half of the row empty, so the remaining link stays anchored to its own edge rather than drifting to the centre.
useWhen: At the foot of a page that sits in a reading order — a guide, a tutorial, a numbered series.
Whenever "what do I read next" has a single obvious answer in each direction.
avoidWhen: To page through a data set — that is `Pagination`, which walks pages of rows and owns a page number. This links two neighbouring documents and knows nothing about a total.
On a page with no reading order (a reference index, a landing page): a next link that points somewhere arbitrary is worse than none.
related: Pagination` — the data counterpart; numbered pages over a collection, not two named documents.
DocOnThisPage` — navigation _within_ the page, where this is navigation _between_ pages.
bestPractices: Pass the destination's real title, not "Next page". The title is what tells the reader whether they want to go.
Leave a side `null` at the ends of a series rather than looping around.
Handle `navigate` when the app routes client-side; the anchor's `href` is what makes the link real for everyone else.

props.name: previousLabel
props.doc: Eyebrow over the previous link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Previous`).

props.name: nextLabel
props.doc: Eyebrow over the next link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Next`).

events.name: navigate
events.notes: Fired when either neighbour is activated; `page` is the side that was clicked. Event first, per `event-payloads.md`.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import DocPagination from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-pagination'
</script>

<template>
  <DocPagination
    :previous="{ title: 'Deploy an application', href: '/docs/deploy' }"
    :next="{ title: 'Bind a domain', href: '/docs/domains' }"
    @navigate="(event, page) => router.push(page.href)"
  />
</template>
